(0:44:41)

And now Brad, let's show. Here are close-ups on those symbols on the top as they appeared on that I-beam, even repeating. And that when you go into early and classic Greek letters, you will find the matched very close to the Greek lambda, the Greek gamma, rho, chi, theta, phi, and this is a repeat on the I-beam of chi and lambda. Now, here is a photograph from another of the 16 millimeter film segments. (0:45:25)

More I-beam debris. And again, these are early Greek symbols. And here, Brad, let's go to the translation. Iota, sigma, eta, theta, in classic Greek. Now, the cameraman, in continuing his story, it's so interesting, he said, I was told to report to Fort Worth, Dallas, for the filming of an autopsy. And normally, I would not have a problem with this, but it was discovered, and he keeps calling them the freaks. (0:46:18)

And here is something that's very puzzling. May be a medical threat. Therefore, I was required to wear the same protective suits as the doctors who did the dissections. So, this is the first time that we hear that they did not do the autopsy anywhere around Roswell. That they must have flown the two bodies that they wanted to do the first two autopsies on, they must have flown it to, as he said, Fort Worth, Dallas. And that he has to put on some kind of a protective garment for a disease. (0:47:02)

And he said it was impossible to handle the camera properly. Loading and focusing was so difficult. But after filming, he said, I had several hundred reels. And I separated the reels and processed them and sent them to Washington. And once the remaining reels had been processed where I was, I contacted Washington to arrange collection of the final batch. (0:47:35)

Get this, this is J.B., quote, incredibly. They, Washington, Wright-Patt, wherever, they never came to collect or arrange transportation. For all of these other film reels that he had taken of the debris and the autopsies. Now, this might seem incredible. But remember, it was exactly at this time in 47, the spring and the summer going to September, that our government was separating the Army and the Air Force. They were being separated into two new branches. (0:48:18)

And there probably was a lot of confusion about turf and what was happening. Because it was September 18, 1947, not long after the July crashes in the May, that Truman officially made the CIA come into being on September 18, 1947. And the Army and the Air Force became these two branches. Everything was moving rapidly. So now, the cameraman says that he did a third autopsy and filmed it in May of 1949. And Ray Santilli told me in his office in London, that after the third humanoid died, and this autopsy was performed, that J.B. was called later, this came later, that J.B. told Santilli that the third autopsy was done quite a bit later and was performed before a gallery of observers at an operating theater in Washington, D.C. An American president, Harry Truman, he thought, secretly attended. (0:49:35)

It is not known if that third dissection was filmed, but it is highly probable that it was. (0:49:44)

Now, what have medical doctors said about filmed alien dissection? I've talked with several who have looked at the Santilli film, and they point out something that's very important when you see the film, which we don't have tonight, but we might as well. Let's go to this next slide, Brad. And in the film, where you can see that everybody said, okay, this is black and white, what was the color of the blood that was oozing from this leg? And when you see the film, and they make a scalpel cut, there is a little bit of oozing along the cut lines, and people wanted to know what the color was in the black and white. (0:50:51)

And J.B. said that the color was the color of blood that we would know, and that the skin of the actual being that he saw was pinkish colored, and that in the live being, and that the one that had been dead when they got to the scene was gray in death, and that these on the fresher autopsies were sort of pinkish gray. (0:51:17)

He said that their skin was lightly mottled in overlapping pink and brown areas, and some of it even looked orange. And he said, in this big stomach that we're looking at, one of the most outstanding anatomical features compared to human bodies is the large protruding stomach. During surgery, a large round mass was found in the very large abdomen above a bunch of other internal organs, but its purpose is unknown. (0:51:57)

I've seen that, and it is a very round, almost bagel-like. And he said further, dark colored tissue that was removed from inside the humanoid head did not resemble normal human brain tissue. And in fact, it was Philip J. Corso and Cooper Anonymous that I interviewed in 1998. Cooper Anonymous told me that he had seen this dissection film, the Santilli dissection film, originally in the 1950s when he was working in cryptoanalysis at a base in the southeastern U.S. And he said when they showed the opening up of the skull of one of these beings that everybody was shocked that it looked like, and he compared it to broccoli. (0:52:54)

Think of broccoli has stems and has all of this articulation on the top, and imagine a brain that had all these branches with all of these articulations like broccoli. That was Cooper's description, and Colonel Corso told me that he agreed. Another part of the medical examination were discovering that these black shiny eyes are really lenses. (0:53:28)

And they discovered this by taking tweezers and lifting off the lens that was covering the eyes. And then when you go to the next image, J.B. said the surgeon is examining what looks like large whites of eyes around a large dark iris that has rolled back in the eye sockets. And that the humanoids, in terms of what they found in the autopsy of the whole body, that these humanoids did not have breasts, a belly button, penis, or testicles. (0:54:07)

But there was an orifice in the pubic area which humans would associate with the female gender, but it was on both of these beings and nothing else was there. And so that's when the doctors concluded that the two beings being autopsied were clones. Now they said also that some chest and heart surgeons, in watching the Santilli film on the autopsies of these beings, that they saw that an object is lifted out of the chest. (0:54:50)

And that doctors in the modern world, upon viewing the Santilli film, said that what they were reminded of was a prosthetic heart valve. (0:54:58)

But Santilli, JB, the film, you can see there's no surgery scar visible on the chest and JB confirmed that with Santilli. So another question is, did the United States government discover the unusual prosthetic device and then back engineer it for application in human medicine and bodies? And that would mean, if that's true, that not everything that has been found in UFO crash debris and been back engineered was weaponized. (0:55:45)

That maybe all along there had been several tracks. It would be DOD and the Black Space Projects and all of the things for weaponizing what they were finding. But they are also, maybe there are intelligent beings that on purpose placed in the hands of humans in the United States and Russia and China. And we know that there are bodies and craft in these other nations as well. (0:56:14)

Clones, androids, on purpose to place some kind of organic advanced prosthetics so that we would start learning how to make them ourselves. And there have been several people that I have talked to who have served in various military and intelligence who said one of the things that became clear early on was that these were not all quote-unquote crashes caused by a thunderstorm or microwave. (0:56:47)

That our government began to catch on. That craft would be placed or made even to look like a crash, but they would decide later that they really weren't crash. It was like a Trojan horse. We're going to put this material so that you can find it and you can safely study it and you can send people to it and you won't be afraid. (0:57:14)

And then we will be guiding you through advancing your technologies by placing so-called crashes around the world. That's perhaps a slice of how complex the entire relationship between Homo sapien, us humans, and other intelligences that have been interacting with our planet for millions of years. And maybe it has been necessary to come to us as crashes, as things that might have scared the government in order to get respect and attention. (0:57:58)

I think these are the big, big questions now that go beyond the 15-page leaked document. The 11-page leaked document about Dr. Kit Green affirming that the Santilli film autopsies are real. That it goes to this bigger question that everybody that I know keeps asking me, and I am waiting impatiently for our government to finally release. And that is, Linda, if all of this is true, then why is not at least the United States government leading the way in announcing we are not alone in this universe, we never have been, that there have been advanced alien intelligences with advanced technologies that can neutralize gravity and do all kinds of interactions in the physical realm and the other dimensional realm and timelines that we have not been able to do. (0:59:18)

And when are we going to get this out in the public? And then would it lead to beings like this? Who are the six-fingered, six-toned, even if they're clones or androids? Who made them? Where are the prime intelligences? (0:59:35)

Which ones are our allies and protecting us? As so many people in military and intel have said, we have allies and they have been protecting us and without them we might be in trouble, but take heart, we have good solid allies. Wow, wouldn't it be fantastic to meet them? Wouldn't it be fantastic to find out who were these six-fingered, six-toes on their mission versus who are the four-fingered, small greys and who are the tall seven to eight feet tall Nordic blondes with the blue eyes and they seem to have five fingers and the reptilians, the reptilians that come with all kinds of descriptions. (1:00:25)

So, to me, the huge value in coming back from the trips where I was talking about these subjects and then reading the 15-page document of notes from Eric Davis, the physicist, and then the 11 pages that are from Eric to Bob Bigelow about Kit Green confirming that the Santilli autopsies are real. I mean, wouldn't you put this in to the category of someone out there is trying to confirm what we keep asking questions and working so hard to understand that we're not alone, this film is real, the notes are real, and the time should be right now that we get that big headline we're not alone. (1:01:39)

So, I know that this has been sort of long and complex and someday maybe we'll have the ability to actually show the whole Santilli film and talk about it as it runs. But I know that I filled this hour and I had intended that this would be a program in which I took you through what I think is so important. (1:02:02)

And that next Wednesday, after I get back from AlienCon, I want to have Lori and Michael, we'll go and do the all questions and hope that you will go out and tell everybody that you know and all of your family to come to the Earth Files YouTube channel for a huge mix of shows on Wednesdays about everything related to this huge question of what kind of universe are we in and what other universes there might be and intelligences. (1:02:35)

And that the issue of subscription, if we can continue to expand our subscriber number, maybe if we get up to 200,000 in July, as I said last week, maybe we won't be interfered with as much by whoever it is that tries to interfere with YouTube broadcasts. And then finally, I am so looking forward to seeing a bunch of you at AlienCon in Los Angeles at the Convention Center starting Friday, Saturday and Sunday this weekend. (1:03:17)

And then I'll be back for a couple of weeks going and then going to Manchester for the Manchester conference that is being held. And I'm going to be doing a presentation there on Spartan 1 and 2. And that then in October will be that UFO cruise that will go from San Diego down south and that will be gone for an entire week. (1:03:41)

And Richard Dolan will be on that cruise and Alan Steinfeld and a bunch of people that I know that it would be so fun if some of you on the other side of this camera would join us in October so that we can all at least pick one night, stay up all night talking about everything that everybody has questions about and then watch the sun come up. entry.title: Colm Kelleher : cattle mutilation は「政府による狂牛病とアルツハイマーの関連調査」だろう
entry.content:
前置き​

これが Colm Kelleher（医学博士）の主張であり、彼の著書でも同様の主張をしていた。過去記事でも取り上げたが、今回は文字起こしも含める。

彼は NIDS/BAAS の一員なので、豊富な情報収集がなされた上での判断だとは思うが、彼の上記のような主張は、まずありえない。低コストかつ合法的にいくらでもサンプルとなる新鮮な牛肉は入手できるゆえ。

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + DeepL(2024-07 model)​

host: 時間がないので、手短にいくつかお聞きします。 あなたの時代に何かが明らかになったのであれば、家畜のミューティレーションと食物連鎖の関係についてお話いただけますか？ （0:39:34）

====

Colm Kelleher: ええ、狂牛病と呼ばれていたものについて、多くの研究が行われていました。英国では、狂牛病（CJD）の経験が明らかに自国のそれ以上のものとなっており、それはアルツハイマー病の診断と重なっています。 結論から言えば、少なくとも米国では、検査を行えば行うほど多くの症例が見つかるため、米国農務省が多くの検査を行う大きな動機付けはありませんでした。 米国では、民間企業が米国政府のために狂牛病プリオン検査を大量に行うことを申し出たという事例がありました。 （0:40:35）

結局、彼らは閉鎖されてしまいました。なぜなら、米国農務省が、その検査を誰にでも公開することを望まなかったからです。結論から言うと、15年後の2021年には、私たちは認知症の大流行に直面しています。認知症には、アルツハイマー病、レビー小体型認知症、前頭側頭型認知症など、さまざまな側面があります。 （0:41:33）

これらの原因を正確に突き止めるのは非常に困難ですが、英国で発生した変異型クロイツフェルト・ヤコブ病の症例は、基本的に、食べたものが病理学的に体に現れるものに影響を与えるという仮説の決定的な証拠となりました。 食物連鎖と認知症の発生には関係があることは疑いの余地がありません。 （0:41:46）

=====

George Knapp: 別の観点から言うと、コルムの本では、誰かが食物連鎖を通じてこれらの病気の蔓延を監視しているように見えると結論づけています。失礼、誰かが蔓延を監視していると。 （0:42:13）

その証拠として私たちが目にするのは、ミューティレーションです。そして、あり得ないことではないのは、複数の何者かによって行われている可能性です。つまり、牛のミューティレーションを取り巻く奇妙な出来事の傘の下に隠れて、何らかの人間組織や団体が牛を切り刻んでいるという可能性です。しかし、それ以上に上位の何者かが、これらの行為を行っている可能性もあります。そして、それが食物連鎖に何があるのかを調べるという現象の起源であり、将来的に本当に大きな問題を引き起こす可能性があるのです。 （0:42:31）

ジョージ、フォローアップもありがとう。

▼原文 展開

I've got a few more questions just before we get to listener questions to finish off. And we'll just kind of fire through these to make the most of it. Can you speak to the possible relationship between cattle mutilations and the food chain, if there was anything that was uncovered during your time? (0:39:34)

Yeah, so there was a lot of research going on between what then was termed mad cow disease. And obviously, the UK had more than its own fair share of experience of mad cow disease, also known as CJD, that overlapped with diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. Bottom line is that in the United States, at least, there was not a great motivator for doing a lot of testing by the USDA because the more you tested, the more cases you would find. So there was a case, there was a situation in the United States where a private company offered to do a whole bunch of BSE, mad cow disease prion testing for the United States government. (0:40:35)

And they were essentially shut down because the USDA did not want to, you know, open the testing to everybody. Bottom line is that, you know, 15 years later, here we are in 2021, we've got a massive epidemic of dementia. And there's multiple aspects of dementia that include Alzheimer's disease, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal lobe dementia, all the way across through the various prion diseases. (0:41:33)

And it is very, very difficult to pin down exactly what the origin of these, but there is, given that the, you know, the UK cases of variant CJD that occurred in the UK were basically the smoking gun for the hypothesis that what you eat will affect what you, what you manifest in terms of pathology. So there is no doubt about it, that there is a relationship between the food chain and the genesis of dementia. (0:41:46)

Just to put it in a different sense, Colum's book concluded that it does appear that somebody is monitoring the spread, excuse me, someone is monitoring the spread of these diseases through our food chain. (0:42:13)

And what we see as evidence of that is mutilations. And the exotic possibility is that it's maybe more than one someone, that some human outfits or organizations are carving up cows, hiding under the umbrella of the weirdness surrounding cattle mutilations to begin with, but that someone else above that is also doing these, these things. And that's where the origin of the phenomena, testing for what's in our food chain, and what might create really bigger problems down the road. (0:42:31)

Thanks for that follow up, George, as well.

entry.title: James Bartley : UFO との遭遇で周囲が霧に覆われたという証言が多数ある （書式変換）
entry.content:
前置き​

James Bartley の講義動画での発言から。

履歴​

(2024-12-06) 書式変換

(2022-05-22) 作成。James Bartley : UFO との遭遇で周囲が霧に覆われたという証言が多数ある

手抜き​

UFO 遭遇で、あたりが霧で覆われたと多くの事例で報告されている。

展開

37:23 the car illuminating the interior of the craft with a pale blue light 37:30 and louise would later recall that the vehicle began to fill with a haze like air a sort of fog and this has also 37:38 been described by other eyewitnesses and in ufo alien encounters

動画(2:32:12)​

Video Lecture About Aliens & Alien Technology for Preston Victoria

コメント​

Xendra の正体は「ドーム状の霧」 (fog dome) だと思うと過去記事で述べたが、その霧は Skinwalker ranch と同様の機序（*1）で地表付近の気温低下が生み出したものではなかろうか。

(*1)​

同様の機序…

強力な EMF 異常が瞬間的に発生すれば下の機序によって気温低下は起きうるのではないか。

  • 急激な EMF 異常 → 大気中の水蒸気もイオン化 → 軽い水素イオンが静電力による反発で急膨張 → 大気温度の急低下 → 水素イオンが再結合し霧が発生

  • この上の機序は以下の過去記事の改訂版に相当。

若干、怪しげな仮説だが、 以下の機序ならドップラー冷却やレーザー冷却といった無理やりな説より、可能性が高そうに思える。それは…

  • 急激な EMF 異常 → 大気分子のイオン化 → 静電力によって大気の分子が反発 → 大気の急激な膨張 → 大気温度の低下

この、EMF 異常による気圧の急低下のメカニズムには、それを支持するデータがひとつある。それは "Oz factor" でよく言われる

  • (a) UFO 出現で、音がくぐもって聞こえた(*2)
  • (b) UFO 出現で、音が変化して聞こえた(*3)

　という報告が、低下した大気圧と耳の内耳圧との差異によってスッキリ説明できる。

また、これまで

  • (c) UFO 出現時に周囲環境が異様に静まり返った

という報告は、意識障害によるものと解釈した(*4)が、「低下した大気圧と耳の内耳圧との差異」も要因になっているのかも。つまり、

  • 音がくぐもって聞こえた → 意識障害中なので、周囲が無音化したという方向に誘導され幻覚がより強化された

という幻覚強化要因となっているとも考えうる。

entry.title: Ray Santilli 自身の証言を含む「ET 解剖動画」の解説動画：文字起こし＋和訳
entry.content:
前置き​

Ray Santilli の「ET 解剖動画」が主題の解説動画。この件を 14年間も調査し続けてきた Philip Mantle の解説的な証言が大半を占める。Ray Santilli （下）自身も顔出しして「あの動画は本物だ」と反論している。

例の制御パネルのシーンや「ET 解剖」の主な動画シーンの引用も含まれている（4:30, 26:00）。

今更言うまでもないが、Ray Santilli の「ET 解剖動画」は明白な捏造。そのシーンの制作担当者本人の証言によって制作過程の細部までが全て明らかとなっている(*1)のだが、少なからぬ著名 UFO 研究者が未練がましく未だに本物だと信じている。

いずれ AI に読ませるために、全発言の文字起こしをつけた。

(*1)​

下の過去記事で取り上げた。

❑ Spyros Melaris の証言 : 「ET 解剖動画」の ET の足は捏造ミスの箇所を隠すためにバーナーで焼いた （途中：1） (2023-07-18)

注目点​

And that's about the gist of it. Forgive me. Is Keith Green saying that the things he saw in the 1980s were similar or the same as the being in the 1995 Santilli film? He emphasises it and actually spells it out in capital letters and says they are the same. Not similar, but the same. And of course, that's simply not possible. (0:44:00)

There are those that think that perhaps, you know, Ray Santilli is not behind the invention of the alien autopsy room, nor is Spiros Melaris, but instead, for some mysterious reason, it's the CIA. There are a number of well-known UFO researchers, primarily in the United States, can't believe that someone of Keith Green's experience and standing would be fooled by a fake film. So there must be something more to it. (0:44:44)

And they believe that he was indeed shown other films, fake or real, by the CIA that look either the same or similar to the Santilli film. Therefore, the CIA must, in some mysterious way, be linked to the faking of it. I can't see any sense in that at all and don't believe a word of it. It is alleged that the CIA have fed false stories about UFOs into the public domain for a variety of reasons. We do know for a fact that they did feed fake UFO sightings into the public domain to cover up overflights of their own spy plane. (0:45:31)

So they may have other reasons for putting fake alien stories into the public domain. If we jump back to Roswell, for example, some people claim that the alien aspect of it is a fake story to cover up what really did happen. But this is only speculation. Here you've got a scientist and a medical doctor being fed information by the CIA. Dr Kit Green, who has now been interviewed by Richard Dolan, has changed his attitude somewhat. (0:46:14)

He believes now the film is a fake and he says that the CIA lied to him back in the 80s. However, he does now still say that some of the film that he saw at the Pentagon, some of the aspects of it, like the creature's face and the hand and the room, were still the same as the Santilli film released in 1995. Now, whether it's the whole film or bits of it, they cannot be the same because the film was only designed and made in 1995. So nothing in it can be the same as something seen back in the 1980s. It is simply not possible. (0:46:58)

When Kit Green does his evaluation, he notices a few small mistakes in the medical procedure. But then, you know, he has an explanation of why these mistakes may have been made, because it was back in 1947. They didn't do things the same then as they do now. And so it was the military, you know, and there are different ways of doing things. He speculates that if any tissue samples were taken, they would go to the Walter Reed Institution, which of course is based at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, which we have mentioned before, and it's linked with UFO research. (0:47:47)

Although he's only speculating, he doesn't know this for sure. It's just pure speculation at that point. When you look at Dr. Kit Green's evaluation of the alien autopsy film, he doesn't get anything right. And you think to yourself, is he looking at the same film as me? (0:48:07)

Because he mentions various medical items in it, which you can't see. You know, they're just not there. So it does make you wonder how he's come to these conclusions. I've tried to get in touch with Mr. Green to ask him a few questions. The first one I would ask is, how did a man of your reputation and experience come to be fooled by this fake film? That would be my first question. (0:48:31)

But unfortunately, I've not had that chance yet. There's a number of things that are important about the memo. It shows you how someone with the knowledge and experience of Dr. Kit Green can be fooled by a piece of film. He wasn't alone. At the time when the film was released around the world, there were a number of physicians who went on the record saying it looks pretty authentic as far as the medical procedures concerned. (0:49:10)

However, they wouldn't comment on what the creature on the slab was. He's gone that one step further. So it just shows you the impact that this film had, not just when it was released, but you know, down the decades and still does continue to have such an impact. I think the biggest revelation is that just when you think you've heard everything there is to hear about the alien autopsy film, and I have a huge archive of material on it, that something else appears and brings it back into the public domain again. (0:49:51)

And the argument starts from scratch. It was almost as if the 14 years I spent investigating it had been a complete waste of time. What is amazing is that Ray Santilli had been quiet for quite a while, but once this email document leaked, he was back on social media saying, I always knew that there were documents somewhere that would prove that what I'd been saying was correct all along. (0:50:22)

He's even done a couple of interviews on a couple of podcasts, still saying I told you I had real film, I told you there was a mysterious cameraman. Well, you know, these documents don't prove anything, but he's using it to the best effect. The Army Air Forces has announced that a flying disk has been found and is now in the possession of the Army. Army officers say the missile, found sometime last week, has been inspected at Roswell, New Mexico, and sent to Wright Field, Ohio for further inspection. (0:50:51)

It's the one case that will not die. It is claimed that not only a UFO crashed, but there were dead alien bodies. It's rumored that perhaps one of those creatures on board did survive for a short period of time. It's the case that will not die. It is shrouded in mystery. And even now, all those that were at Roswell or saw something around the time have all passed away. (0:51:15)

However, information still comes to light. It's lying in somebody's files or in a cupboard or, you know, in the attic in a box. You know, just when you think you've heard everything there is to know about Roswell, something pops up and bites you on the backside. It really does. (0:51:32)

(2024-12-05)

entry.title: Anthony Peake: 側頭葉癲癇発生時に予知が起きた。それを目撃した
entry.content:
前置き​

Anthony Peake が目撃体験を証言している。この件は過去記事でも取り上げた(*1)が、今回は和訳をつける。

DeepL 訳が使い物にならないレベルだったので、肝心の部分だけは ChatGPT-4o に訳を依頼した。

ついでに、この動画全体の 文字起こし＋和訳 もつけた。

(*1)​

Anthony Peake：私の眼の前で、癲癇患者が一瞬先の未来を正確に予知した。 （途中：その1） (2018-05-19)

❏ Anthony Peake : 癲癇 による時間停止体験 （途中 1） (2024-06-02)

Anthony Peake：側頭葉癲癇患者が体験した時間経過の超緩慢化現象（途中：その2） (2018-05-19)

❏ ドストエフスキー（癲癇）の描写：発作が引き起こした「全てを知った」という感覚 (2023-12-11)

Anthony Peake : 癲癇が「この現実の裏側に存在するリアリティ」を認知するドアを開いた。（途中：その2） (2020-03-21)

側頭葉癲癇患者の驚くべき体験談：周囲の時間がほとんど停止状態になった　（途中：その1） (2017-06-29)

さまざまな「時間経過が遅く感じる体験」（途中：その1） (2015-02-21)

Anthony Peake : Emanuel Swedenborg の癲癇と予知（途中：その1） (2014-08-10)

関連​

❏ Ivana Radovniković と Anthony Peake の対話：全発言＋日本語訳 (2023-12-07)

Anthony Peake：シャルル・ボネ症候群やアルツハイマーの患者に、グレイや小人・妖精が出現している。　（途中：その1） (2018-05-18)

Anthony Peake：脳は意識を生み出さない。脳は意識のリミッターだ。 (2018-05-16)

Desta Barnabe : 100% 現実で、完全に目覚めて体験していると実感 → 後に現実ではないと判明 (2021-07-23)

"Astral Projection"/OBE ：我々はこの現実世界から「真の世界」を垣間見るのか、それとも「真の世界」から現実世界に一時的に潜り込んでいるのか？ (2021-07-19)

Tom Campbell : この「虚構の現実世界」の外側に真の世界があり、意識はそこに属している。 (2021-05-20)

Anthony Peake : 脳内グリア細胞は量子力学的な非局在効果で通信し、アカシック・レコードにアクセスする。 (2019-06-30)

Anthony Peake：この現実世界の奥に隠れた真実の世界があり、それを垣間見ることができる。 (2018-06-13)

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + ChatGPT-4o​

そして、あなたが戻ってきた。そして、マーガレットが言っていたんだが、彼女（マーガレット）はかなり長い間不在だった。その後、彼女は神経学的な検査を受け、側頭葉てんかんだと診断された。そこから数年が経った頃、私は最初の本を書いた。

その本を書く際、私は側頭葉てんかん（TLA）の要素について深く掘り下げた。そして、ジェーン・バートンという女性から連絡をもらった。彼女は看護師で、その時イギリスてんかん協会の非常に高い地位にいて、たしかその会長だったと思う。彼女自身も長年にわたって側頭葉てんかんを患い、脳の一部を切除する手術を受けるほどだった。

彼女は「WADAテスト」を受けたり、さまざまな検査を受けたりして側頭葉てんかんを調べてきた。そして彼女はこう言った。「お会いできませんか？」その頃、私はマージーサイドのウィラルに住んでいて、スピーク空港の近くで仕事をしていた。そこは市中心部から6～7マイルほど離れた場所だった。

マーガレットもジェーンも、「あなたの近くのショッピングセンターで会いましょう」と言ってきた。ジェーンは「そこにはとても素敵なボーダーズ書店があって、そこで会いましょう」と言った。

私たちは会う約束をした。そして、ジェーンがやって来た。そのボーダーズ書店のレイアウトを説明すると、店の奥には中二階があり、そこにはコスタコーヒーがあった。そのコーヒーショップは、店全体と入り口を見下ろすようなバルコニーになっていた。

ジェーンが到着し、席についてコーヒーを渡すと、彼女はこう話し始めた。「リバプールの中心部までバスで息子とその友達を連れてきたの。それで彼らをそこに残してから、バスでここに来たの。終わったらまたバスでリバプールの中心部に戻って、息子たちと合流して帰る予定よ」と。

彼女はそう説明した後、突然話を止めて、じっと私を見つめた。その瞬間、彼女が「小発作（ペティ・マル）」に入ったのだと分かった。

彼女が意識を取り戻すと、店の入り口の方向を見てこう言った。「あれ？なんであの人がここにいるの？おかしいわ。ここにいるはずないのに。リバプールで会うって言ったのに。」そう言った後、また意識を戻した。

私は「小発作（今はこの言葉を使わないけど）を起こしましたよ」と言おうとしたところ、彼女は店の入り口を再び見て、また同じ言葉を繰り返した。そして、その瞬間、息子とその友人が店の入り口から入ってきたのだ。

私は、自分の目と耳でその出来事を目撃した。彼女は、自分の人生でこれから起こることを即座に認識していた。彼女はこう言った。「こういうことがよく起こるんです。でも、誰かに実際に目撃されたのは初めてです」と。

この出来事は、意識の変容状態がどれほど魅力的で、驚くべき可能性を秘めているかを示す非常に特別な証拠だと思いました。

AI の解釈​

Me: 先の事例は 1. 彼女の息子たちが出現するタイミングが、若干早まった 2. 彼女がたまたま息子が出現する直前にその（息子たちの出現の）幻覚を見た …この 1 と 2 が合致した稀なケースだというのがまぁ、普通の解釈になりますよね。

ChatGPT-4o

おっしゃる通りです。それが合理的で科学的な解釈になると思います。具体的には以下のようなシナリオが考えられます：

1. タイミングの偶然性​

  • 息子たちが現れたタイミングが、彼女の発作や幻覚の直後だったという偶然が起きた。
  • 側頭葉てんかんの影響で、彼女の認知や意識が「直前の幻覚」と「直後の現実」とを関連付けてしまった可能性があります。

2. 発作中の幻覚​

  • 彼女が発作中に見た幻覚（息子たちが現れるイメージ）は、実際には発作が引き起こした脳の活動にすぎない。
  • 息子たちが来ること自体は事前に計画されており（「リバプールで会う」など）、潜在的な記憶が幻覚として再構成された可能性があります。

3. 偶然の一致​

  • 息子たちの実際の到着タイミングが、彼女の幻覚の後にちょうど一致したという稀なケース。これは統計的には起こり得る範囲の「偶然」と考えられます。
  • こうした出来事が「予知」と解釈されるのは、人間の脳がパターン認識や因果関係を過剰に結びつける傾向があるためです。

4. 普通の解釈としてのまとめ​

  • **息子たちの到着（現実）**と、**幻覚的な先見（発作の影響）**が偶然合致した。
  • 彼女が「よくこういうことがある」と言ったのは、実際には過去の記憶や潜在的な予想が発作の間に「未来」として感じられた可能性があります。

こうした偶然は非常に印象的で「奇跡的」に思えるため、予知として語られることが多いですが、科学的な視点から見ると、脳の異常な活動とタイミングの偶然によるものと解釈するのが自然です。

とはいえ、この事例が語られることで、人間の意識や脳の不思議さを再認識させられるのもまた事実ですね。

上記部分と別の事例を含む部分の DeepL 訳​

▼展開 DeepL 訳（意味不明）

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + DeepL(2024-07 model)​

最初の出来事は1999年から2000年にかけてのことだった。本を書くことは決めていたのですが、その本のテーマが何なのかわかりませんでした。 そして研究を始めるうちに、側頭葉てんかんという病状と臨死体験の間に信じられないようなつながりがあることを発見した。特に、臨死体験をしたときに影響を与える神経伝達物質と、側頭葉てんかんを患っている人の間につながりがあることがわかった。側頭葉てんかんとデジャ・ヴュ、そして側頭葉てんかんがデジャ・ヴュの感覚を促進するような仕組みです。 (0:02:26)

実際、これは側頭葉てんかん患者のオーラ状態と呼ばれるものの一部です。ある日の午後、リクルートのコンサルタント会社から電話がかかってきた。私はその女性をマーガレットと呼んだ。これは彼女の名前ではないが、身元を守るためにこう呼んでいる。 (0:02:43)

そして彼女は私に電話をかけてきて、あなたのために契約の可能性があると言いました。この契約の面接に来ていただけませんか？ ガトウィック空港です。とても興味があるかもしれない。そして、私は振り返って、いや、私は本を書くために1年間休暇を取ることに決めたので、特に興味はないと答えた。 そしていつものように、誰かにそう言うと、彼女は振り返って言った。と聞かれたので、よくわからないんです。どこに行こうとしているのかわからないんだ。 (0:03:05)

でも今のところ、私は側頭葉てんかんと側頭葉てんかんの影響について研究しているんだ。彼女はとても静かになって、ああ、それは興味深いね、と言った。 コーヒーを飲みに行きませんか？私はもちろんそうしましょうと答えた。数日後、ガトウィック空港近くのホテルでコーヒーをご一緒しましょう。 (0:03:28)

それで僕は、うん、わかった、いいよ、と答えた。そこで私は彼女と待ち合わせ、彼女は席に着き、その間に私にコーヒーをおごってくれた。あなたをここに招待したのは、オフィスでは言えなかったんだけど、最近TLEと診断されたからなんです。と彼女は言った。そして、彼女が言っていたことの多くが、私自身の経験と重なるのだ。 (0:03:51)

それで私は、わかった、例えばどんなこと？すると彼女は、私の本の方向性に対する私の考えを大いに刺激するようなことを言ったんだ。数週間前、彼女はクライアントと一緒にいて、クライアントの工場を訪ねたんだ。 (0:04:11)

そして彼女は、彼女、彼女の友人、彼女のクライアントは、彼らのためにお茶を2杯持ってきていて、彼らには急須があったと言った。そしてその客は自分用にお茶を注ぎ始めた。そうしているうちに、マーガレットは左耳の上でパチンと音がしたのを感じた。 (0:04:27)

そして彼女は、彼女の友人か、彼女が会いに行った問題の女性が動かなくなっ ていることに気づいた。そして彼女は文字通り、空間の中で固まっていた。そして、低いハミングのような音が聞こえてきた。そして、彼女はもう一人の女性の動きが止まっていないことに気づいた。

(0:04:55)

そして彼女は、聞こえていたハミング音が周囲の人々の声であることに気づいた。そして彼女は、文字通り、時間の認識が本当に変わったと言った。彼女は時間の認識がまったく違っていた。そして彼女は私の方を振り向き、とても重要なことを言った。紅茶が紅茶の表面に当たるのを見たんです。 (0:05:19)

そして私はそれが飛び散るのを見た。そして初めて表面張力を見た。私はすべてを見た。そして彼女は言った、そして長い間離れていたことに気づいた。まるで時間が止まってしまったかのように感じた。どれくらい離れていたと思う？数分、数時間、数年、あるいは一生かもしれない。 (0:05:36)

そして彼女は言った、まるで一生を過ごしたかのように思えた後、また私の耳にパチンと音がした。もう一人の女性は動き続け、お茶を注ぎ続け、彼女を見た。マーガレットは言った。どんなふうに？と聞くと、マーガレットは、どんな風に？ (0:05:58)

それからあなたは戻ってきた。マーガレットが私に言ったように、彼女は非常に長い間離れていた。そして彼女は神経学的検査を受け、実際に側頭葉てんかんであることがわかった。それから数年が経った。私は初めて本を書いた。 最初の本を書いたとき、私はTLAの多くの要素に焦点を当てた。そして、ジェーン・バートンという女性から連絡をもらった。ジェーン・バートンは看護師で、当時はたしかUKてんかん協会の会長だった。彼女は側頭葉てんかんを長年患っていて、脳の一部を摘出したほどでした。 (0:06:41)

彼女はWADAテストを受けた。側頭葉てんかんの検査もいろいろやってもらった。そして彼女は、あなたのために会うことはできますか？当時、僕はマージーサイドのウィラルに住んでいた。当時、私はスピーク空港の近くでビジネス契約をしていて、市街地から6、7マイルほど離れた郊外にいた。 とマーガレットが言うと、ジェーンは、あなたの地元のショッピングセンターで会いましょう、と言った。 (0:07:10)

それで会う約束をした。彼女はボーダーズの店のレイアウトを説明するために現れた。 店の奥には中二階があった。そして店の奥にはコスタのコーヒーショップがあり、バルコニーから他の店や店の入り口が見渡せるようになっていた。 (0:07:32)

それでジェーンがやってきて、座って、私は彼女にコーヒーを出して、彼女は座って、私に向かってこう言ったんです。私たちが終わったら、またバスに乗ってリバプールの中心部まで戻るわ。 (0:07:52)

そして彼女は言った、そして彼女は私にこれら全てを説明した、そして突然彼女は立ち止まり、私を見つめた。 (0:07:58)

そして彼女は中二階の上から店の入り口の方を見て、ああ、彼はここで何をしているの？彼はここにいるべきじゃない。そんなバカな。彼はここで何をしているの？私は彼にリバプールで会うと言い、彼女はまた戻ってきた。 そして、私は彼女に、あなたは今、些細なマル......を持っていたと言うために振り向くところだった。もうプチ欠神発作という言葉は使わなくていい。 (0:08:26)

そして彼女は私に返事をしようとした時、ふと目をやり、店の入り口のドアを見て、息子とその友人がドアから入ってくるのと全く同じ言葉を発した。 私はこの目で見て、この耳で聞いた。 というのも、彼女は私にこう言ったからだ。よくあることだと彼女は言ったが、本当に誰かに目撃されたのは今回が初めてだと。 (0:09:02)

これは私にとって、意識の変容状態がいかに魅力的なものであるかを示す、特別な証拠であった。

動画(1:39:27)​

INCON with Dr Louise Spiers

www.youtube.com/watch?v=yA5oO15gIOU

動画概要欄​

600 views 2023/08/07 Below is the link to Dr Spiers' survey.

おまけ：全発言文字起こし＋和訳​

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + DeepL(2024-07 model)

▼展開 和訳

So what they're doing is they're looking at the chemical reactions and the way certain neurochemicals and the way serotonin does this and dopamine does this, but they're never actually thinking, but what is serotonin? What is serotonin acting upon? It's a chemical, but it's acting upon something that is an epiphenomenon of brain brain structure, which is consciousness. But you know, as you know, 1994 when the Australian philosopher, I can't remember now which his name is, just slipped my mind for a second. (1:21:37)

But you know, when he came up with the hard problem of consciousness, you know, how does inanimate matter in the brain create you and me? You know, there's no answer to that. We still are no close to that billion dollar question, but this then extrapolates into experience. It extrapolates into the way we see the world. There's so many things here that we need to deal with in one way or another, you know, and I find it quite frustrating that we've still got eliminative materialists. (1:22:11)

We've still got people like Daniel Dennett and the Churchlands that are completely convinced that we have no inner life at all. It's an hallucination. We are fooling ourselves into thinking we are even self-aware. I mean, what a nonsensical statement. Every single sentient human being on the planet can dismiss that statement in a second. (1:22:35)

But it's still their religion. It's still their viewpoint, you know. And I hope that work like the stuff you're doing. And I still think that extraordinary human experiences facilitated by things like temporal lobe epilepsy are going to be the things that are going to break us through into the new area. (1:22:53)

And I really hope so. And I mean, you know, Oliver Sacks, he was very generous. You talked about his book Hallucinations. I think the way that he talks about the experiences of individuals who have these kind of exceptional experiences was actually the most generous and the kindest that I've seen in print. Because he talks about how these kinds of experiences can tell us something about our humanity. (1:23:19)

They can tell us something about what it's like to be a human being at all, let alone in a non-consensual reality. (1:23:29)

Because they're like aesthetic experiences, he says, if we can, you know, if we can think of them like that, then what is beauty? Well, nobody tries to find out. Well, actually, they are now starting to look at where in the brain it might say that. But it's nonsense to say, where in the brain might you find your love of Monet? You know, that's, yeah. (1:23:57)

In the impressionist cortex, probably. Yeah, very good. Yeah. So I, yeah, I suppose. How did I deal with it? It's a really good. It's a really good, good question. A lot of a lot of the way that I actually that I that I have dealt with this is is through hearing such honest and brave testimony of the people who I interviewed of my participants. (1:24:43)

And that has given me a bit of bravery to be a bit more out there and talk about it a lot more. Yeah, I think I think that has that has really helped. One of the things I'd just like to put something from the chat room, which I think is really quite fascinating, that it'd be really interesting to to think about. (1:24:58)

And Sarah, I could draw you in on this one. Evolving Spirit says, I have aphantasia, no mental images whatsoever, no colours, just black. I wonder what would happen if I took ayahuasca or DMT? That's a fascinating thing, isn't it? If you have no inner imagery. As far as I understand it, you have a psychedelic experience without any visual imagery. But also aphantasia is different for different people. (1:25:24)

So some people do have visual imagery in their dreams. So in which case, if they took ayahuasca, quite likely that they would have visual imagery. And it depends whether it's something that they've been born with or something that's developed over time, because I do think it's also an aspect of what's being called digital dementia now as well, where people don't have such good visual mental imagery. (1:25:46)

So yeah, it is interesting. I guess you could describe... So digital dementia, can you expand on that for a second? Digital dementia is where people are having the kind of cognitive decline associated with the sorts of cognitive decline you'd get in much older people, as a result of using media and digital devices so much that they aren't using their own mental cognitive functions, and therefore it's kind of atrophying to some extent. (1:26:13)

Have you got any opinion on that, Louise? That was really fascinating. That's terrifying, isn't it? That is terrifying. I do know someone who has that condition, actually, not the digital one. And although they don't have a visual experience, they do experience energy. So when having an altered state, they will experience shifts in energy and emotional emotions and feelings. (1:26:48)

But that's also how if you have aphantasia, you experience dreams quite often. It's like you have an emotional sense of feeling, even an idea that something's there, but not sort of clear, lucid visual imagery. (1:26:56)

Yeah, yeah. So there is a connection. Yeah, there is a connection to something, even if you don't see anything. Yeah. Fear not, person in the chat room. Absolutely. So what's your intentions now with the research when you've got it all together? What are you going to do with it? Well, a few years ago, just before COVID, I spoke at an international congress of psychiatrists who were interested in spirituality. (1:27:33)

And part of the feedback that I got from that was, this is really interesting, but you're only talking about a really small number of people. And actually, we need to know, is this prevalent? So what I'd like to do is take this big body of survey respondents and then put that out there into the world. (1:28:07)

I'm going to talk with, I'm involved with an epilepsy charity in the UK. So I'd like to get out there to their members, but also through their professional membership, talk to neuropsychiatric individuals, epilepsy nurses, like the lady that you were involved in, they're epilepsy nurse specialists, and publish this so that I can get a conversation started, really, in the literature. (1:28:43)

One of the things that probably some people are not aware of is that I worked for 18 months at Young Epilepsy, which is a school very close to where I live here in Lingfield, in Surrey. And that was really quite fascinating, because I used to speak to the psychiatrists there, and the neurologists and various other people. But what was really fascinating was talking to the people who were responsible for the children in the school and in the college and in the little units, because what they did was they'd have houses, and they'd have about five or six children or young adults living together in these circumstances. (1:29:22)

And I used to spend opportunities talking to the heads of the houses. And they told me that they regularly witnessed telepathy. They regularly witnessed the fact that even though there were no clocks on the walls, the children knew exactly what time it was. There were also a number of children who had severe autism, and some of the abilities that the autistic children had were absolutely uncanny. (1:29:47)

And I said, so would you generally say your consensus of opinion is what skills do these children have? And they said, phenomenal. We just need to channel it in some way, because it's extraordinary. The things we witness on a daily basis are extraordinary. And wouldn't it be amazing if, I mean, Perfinger talks about how it could be the source of sigh. Wouldn't that be amazing? Yeah, no, absolutely. (1:30:12)

And I'm reminded when you were talking there, a few years ago, I was doing quite a lot of research on schizophrenia. And I wrote a book on the near-death experience with a guy called Dr Mahendra Perera, who's an Australian psychiatrist. And he, when he was studying, he, when he did his PhD, rather than his doctor's degree, he studied on, he specialised in schizophrenia. (1:30:35)

And he worked with a guy called Alex Jenner, who was Professor of Psychiatry at Leeds University. And he put me in contact with Alex. And I had the opportunity to have a very long chat with one of the world's leading experts on schizophrenia. This guy had spent 45 years of his life researching schizophrenia and allied experiences, you know, like TLA and everything else. (1:31:00)

And I asked him, and I said, so you're one of the world's leading experts on schizophrenia. What is it? And he said, I've absolutely no idea. He said, all I know is it is not one typology. There are so many different facets of this. We've lumped it together because we have no idea what it is. And I would argue that within my Huxleyan spectrum, I would argue that the same can be said for the schizophore epilepsy, isn't there, on the extremes of epilepsy, there's the schizophore elements. (1:31:28)

And I know that my friend Myron Dial overlaps into that area. And as he said, you know, and Myron has been on this show a couple of times, you know, that the doors of perception are so open for these individuals that they can't even function correctly because there's so much information coming in. The filters just aren't working anymore. (1:31:51)

The filters have gone. They've blown off. So no wonder they act erratically. It's because they can't deal with it. And I think, you know, that we could pull into here, as I say, autism and various other things, because I think a lot of these areas, they have elements of each other in one way or another. (1:32:10)

And we need to think, well, you know, where's the feedback mechanisms taking place here? What can this tell us? Instead of compartmentalising them, let's re-look at them again and let's talk to the people who experience them. That's what you should be doing. That's what that's what you're doing. And that's why your work is so important. (1:32:32)

You know, absolutely. Right. I'm aware of getting towards the end now. So, Louise, can you let us know how anybody that's fascinated by this can contact you, check out your website, everything else? So where can they come to? (1:32:42)

So I can be contacted on louise.spires at northampton.ac.uk, my university address, and the university also holds details of my research. So if somebody looks up Louise Spires Northampton University, then they will see they will see the details. That's no problem. I guess that you hold details on your website. Yeah, I will. I will put up the links as well. (1:33:27)

Yeah, because the the the link for the for the research, which I can put in the chat room, is quite long. So so whilst I can read it out for people, whilst they're desperately scribbling it down, I'll put it in the chat. Well, no, because it's sort of been recorded anyway. That's probably the best way or contact me. (1:33:49)

Yeah. And it's also if you're if you're really desperate and you can't remember my name and how to get there, then Epilepsy Action, who I'm working with, they've been very supportive, actually. And they've got the survey advertised on their research page as well. So you can always go in through Epilepsy Action's research page and they have it advertised to. Wonderful. So that's the way to do it. (1:34:12)

Wonderful, because funnily enough, Myron's just made a comment from America. No doctor has ever explained my experiences. I just have them. Sorry about that. And it's true, isn't it? You know, it's the trying to compartmentalize the extraordinary. Yeah. And that's not. It's not my desire. My desire is to say, aren't we aren't we wonderful? Don't we all have access to something amazing? And and shouldn't that be honored? Absolutely. Is there anything that we've missed that you think from our conversation that you'd like to mention now or anything or, you know, do you feel? Oh, goodness me, no. (1:34:50)

I think we've spoken about so much and I could talk forever about this stuff. I don't know about you, but it's so it's it's and and the crossover, I think, with different conditions. People are always asking me, I have schizophrenia. Do you think it's like this? I think, you know, people who are non neurotypical have a different way of engaging. Sarah, have you got any final points? I also think neurotypical is a bit of a misnomer, really, because everyone's like an individual fingerprint and we're bound to be the same neurologically as we are fingerprint wise as well. (1:35:33)

So I don't think this idea of being neurotypical holds that much water. And actually, you know, we've said it before so many times on this show in terms of especially neuroscience, the materialist reductionist view of neuroscience as being that the character of a person, the emotional state of a person, the psychology of a person can be determined by just looking at that brain is not even scientific anyway. (1:35:56)

And so if we're getting to a point in science where we're recognising the interconnectedness of species, let's say through mycelial networks, then I think we're going to start to understand that human beings have a similar, perhaps not yet visible or well understood mycelial network themselves and that we're all interconnected. (1:36:15)

And that's actually a much more scientific way to look at life on this planet. And this also means that we can, like you say, honour those kinds of experiences as being perhaps sometimes overwhelming, uncomfortable and unpleasant experiences of too much information coming in simultaneously where someone can't function. And therefore, you know, I have friends that have a lot of issues whereby they experience really scary psychotic breaks and this kind of stuff. And I don't think you want to downplay that in terms of and also the same sort of delusions of grandeur and Jesus complex and this kind of stuff. (1:36:51)

Like, I think everything needs to be looked at on an individual basis, bearing in mind that we're all connected at the same time, so that the understanding that we're part of this interconnected cosmos can inform and educate the experience of an individual and that the reality of us all being interconnected is modulated through an individual's understanding and perception of the world. (1:37:17)

So it's fed by the culture of that person as they grow up and that changes the way they view these anomalous experiences, I think, quite often. But I do think, you know, it's interesting that you brought up Zikiku because I study ancient dreaming cultures and Zikiku means ghost or spirit in Sumerian and it relates to a book of dream omens, a series of dream omens, the Ishkar Zikiku. And in Babylonia, you wouldn't just have a physical physician doctor, you'd also have an Ashiku, a spirit doctor. (1:37:51)

So there's always been an awareness of spirit and if we were to return to a culture where we acknowledged that human beings even have a spirit and that we're part of a divine conscious cosmos, then we wouldn't have these problems in the first place. Culture is sick and the world is sick and society is sick and I think we'd probably find there'd be a lot less sick individuals if our culture and our society wasn't so sick. (1:38:19)

Well said. Well said, Sarah. Very impressive. That's good. Right, okay, very much. Thanks everybody for listening in. As usual, this has been recorded and it will go up as a recording tomorrow and then it will be up there for permanent viewing. So if anybody wants to watch this again, and I'm sure many people will, you have the opportunity there. Also, if you can share it with as many people as you possibly can, because this is Louise's work is incredibly important, as we've tried to stress, and it's important that we get this out there as well. Just let everybody know that at the moment our next guest will be on the 13th of August and we've got Rizwan Virk joining us from California, which means that we'll be going out slightly later. (1:39:02)

So we'll probably go out around about eight o'clock UK time and he'll be joining us from there. And this is going to be a fascinating discussion on the latest research in terms of the true nature of reality and everything else as well. So if you can join us for that, that would be really wonderful. (1:39:18)

So everybody, thanks very much again and we'll speak to you soon. Okay, thanks very much and goodbye again. And my thanks again to Sarah and thanks again to Louise for a wonderful discussion. Bye. (1:39:26)

(2024-12-05)

entry.title: 「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の謎を解く （途中1）
entry.content:
前置き​

Ryan Burns は Skinwalker ranch の南側に隣接した土地を購入して所有しており、"Space Wolf Reserch" と名付けている。

その所有地で起きた「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の事件を取り上げ、その謎を解く(*1)。

これまでも「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」について多数の報告があり、証拠の 写真/動画 のデータも提示されてきた。それらのデータから「Bigfoot が portal（異次元空間ゲート） の類を通って 別次元/別空間 へ移動したのだ」…的な解釈が横行している。

だが、今回の動画で提示されている状況証拠から全く別の合理的な機序があることに気付いた。この動画撮影者を含め、誰一人としてこの機序に気づいていない筈（DoD や情報機関の一部は気づいているかも）。

なお、ここでは

敷地に設置した 4トンのコンテナが勝手に移動した ⇒ この謎を解く

という事件も起きている。

(*1)​

途中で途切れる Bigfoot の足跡の謎とその解明については、

Missing-411 や Bigfoot : 足跡が途中で途絶える現象 → 合理的に説明する （途中2） (2023-02-23)

❑ 発見される Bigfoot の足跡の殆どが一つだけで、それも 99% が右足である理由 （＋追加 1） (2023-07-19)

で取り上げたが、本記事の事例では上の過去記事の謎解きの適用はかなりの無理がある。

だが、本記事の事例は全く別の合理的な説明が可能なので、それを以下で説明する。たぶん、捏造を除けば大部分の「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の事例では以下の機序で説明できる筈。

Attention! Alright, you'll be alright. My grandfather, too, he would tell the same story. In that same area, there was a horse, like a horseman. So, there definitely is that creature out there. Last year, I assembled a team of like-minded guys to come with me on a quest to document and even possibly experience some of these mysterious phenomena for ourselves. In the summer of 2022, the team got a chance at a trip of a lifetime when a show guest named Ryan invited us to his property called Space Wolf Research. Located in Utah's Uintah Basin, at the very doorstep of the infamous Sherman Ranch, Space Wolf had already produced multiple reports and evidence of strange happenings from skinwalkers to UFOs. Really? Had a blanket over their head and came towards the truck. And I rolled down the window and said, hey, you want to get in? We arrived somewhere. They thought I was drunk. Did all the tests. They realized I wasn't. And asked me what happened. And when I told them, they explained to me that I had been nabbed by the skinwalker. And that's the first time I'd ever heard that. Seeking answers after his own encounter, Ryan would purchase property bordering the Sherman Ranch and attempt to create what he would refer to as a safe haven of sorts for the phenomena. (0:04:05)

No guns, no threats. (0:04:07)

So Ryan wants to create a safe haven for all the activity in the area. So, you know, if this stuff is conscious and it's bobbing and weaving and ducking behind bushes or whatever trying to avoid human contact, well, he wants to create an environment on his properties where it's just like a place where consciously it's known to be a safe place where nothing's going to happen, you're not going to get shot at kind of thing. (0:04:32)

So whether it's Bigfoot, shadow entities, aliens, UFOs, portals, they're welcome on his property. So he has a no-gun policy. He doesn't want anybody having guns on the property. Since episode 202, I've become pretty friendly with Ryan and I respect him. So we're going to follow his orders and his wishes and we're going to do this gun-free. So it's going to be interesting. Hopefully nothing too crazy happens that we can't handle with a hatchet, but we'll see. (0:05:01)

So show us the picture that we got. Oh, yeah. So apparently Christian's already there. And when they got to the ranch, one of the shipping containers that's on the property was picked up and moved. But there was no drag marks when it was moved and there was no tire tracks, nothing around. It was just mysteriously moved. So this is the picture that was sent right here. (0:05:35)

Oh, I got it, I got it. That's the picture right there, which is nuts. And you can tell there's no drag marks, like it was slid. It was just picked up in the middle of the night and moved. There was nothing on the property. So, yeah, this is what we're walking into. Teleporting shipping containers and we haven't even got there yet. So I feel like we're on track to see some wild stuff, I can tell you that. (0:06:05)

I appreciate your time. Oh, thank you. No problem. As part of my duty here, you know, I'm security. Right. So anything that happens out here, I'm supposed to be on top of it. I am absolutely baffled with how a 9,000 pound container is moved. Not so much as a blade of grass disturbed. Because there's no... it looks like it was picked up and moved. (0:06:40)

There's no scraping. Wasn't it by the building? Right by the building? Yeah, it was next to the building and now it's the other way. It's turned, isn't it turned? It's completely turned as if it was lifted. I didn't notice that. But I came out here and I go... Oh. That gray container was right here. Correct. And no skid marks, it's been skid by, right? (0:07:03)

That end right there was right there. I mean, a couple of years before, there was a 40 foot RV almost exactly where the container was that was vaporized by what was apparently a daytime lightning bolt. Well, we have pictures of the lightning strike. Ryan has them and I got them too. And they estimated that a 12 foot bolt hit the trailer and melted it. (0:07:29)

The lightning was getting kind of close and I told my husband, we better go in the house. (0:07:33)

I was getting pretty close and then boom, it hit right across the street. And we called the fire department and it was melted down, that whole trailer, within seconds. It went like this. So it had to be lifted up. Yeah. Here's a little bit of evidence. It wasn't lifted that high because it caught this rock. Look it. It caught that rock and it caught this one. (0:08:01)

It caught those three. It caught those rocks and moved them. But it had to be up high. What would it take to melt metal into rock? I mean, would a lightning bolt do that? Alright, so we've been here at this location for, I don't know, like six hours. You're going to freak out when you get here. There's some stuff that's totally unexplainable already. (0:08:32)

Really? Yeah, we've met some of the neighbors. They told us stuff that's going to blow your mind. Let me tell you this. Some of the words that we were told. Giant red-headed cannibals. Giant red-headed what? What? Woo! Hold on a sec. Giant red-headed what? Let's go, baby! But one of the Native American Indians that we've been hanging out with here told us about giant red-headed cannibals. (0:09:03)

You'll learn more about that. Water babies that are evil. What? Yeah. And what do you call star people? Star people. The star people that fly. Let's go! Oh, let's go. Well, just trying to find some gas before we run out of gas. Nothing major to see here. Where are we, Tony? I honestly don't know. Kansas, I believe? This is Wakini. Wakini? This is downtown Wakini. Downtown Wakini is closed. (0:09:39)

How we doing? Oh, fantastic. Yeah. Fantastic. You get killed by a serial killer before we even get there. Yeah. Geez, we're not worried about the skinwalkers. We're worried about getting picked up in Wakini by the guy from So I Know What You Did Last Summer, you know? Wakini looks like a waste. There's nothing going on here. I've never seen this empty of a town. (0:10:17)

That's what the Wakini Whacker wants you to think. With Christian and Joseph already reporting sightings, we raced through the night to get there. As the rest of the crew continued our 30-hour drive, they settled in for their first night at Space Wolf Research. But as we've always heard, when the sun goes down, the land comes alive. I came out here to produce a movie. (0:10:52)

I didn't plan on being in a movie. I've seen these shows. I'm a filmmaker. But when you have a real experience, like when we were looking through the binoculars and you shot that film through your iPhone and then you blew it up. I don't know what that was flying through. But then last night, that was it, man. I don't... I just... I don't... Listen, if he doesn't want to pay... I don't know. (0:11:26)

I need some coffee, though. Maybe I'll feel different. But last night, that was... there was a constant... it wasn't a hum. (0:11:34)

It was more like a rolling growl. Like... like a... It was like if the valley was snoring. It just... it just kept going and going. So much so that I got out of my tent and I went and slept in my truck. Arriving in Utah, we knew we would be walking into a very active situation. Not only had Christian and Joseph had a rough first night, but according to locals, the last few days had seen a spike in activity on the property. (0:12:06)

Finally pulling into our campsite at Space Wolf, we all felt heaviness and the surreal realization that we stood on the doorstep of one of the most infamous hubs of high strangeness in the world. Well, the first thing we did when we got here is we set up, looking out at the mesa there, the binoculars on a tripod. And we were just hanging out looking and I saw, and you'll see right across here, is some big solar panels. (0:12:40)

But from here at first it looked like a truck. And then there's a big tower... and what we figured out is at night it's solar panels that charge the light. And so as at night there's a red light and a white light and the white light turns... it blinks. I think it's so maybe some flames don't hit the mesa or I don't know. (0:12:58)

But then Christine and I were like, let's see if we can hold our camera up to the lens of the binoculars. And he started shooting and then I said, did you get that? So as I was talking earlier, down there, we're talking like this was a form of warfare, you know. So that was the purpose of it. So they do carry medicine from that realm. (0:50:30)

This is all energized, they're all sponsored from this dark realm, from a specific point. So they do have the ability to hurt people, to kill people, to take things from people. It's all about control. I don't know exactly, I try not to know, but you know, it's all around us. We hear a lot of things. I don't know, you know, it's just a bad, dark place for bad, dark people, you know. (0:51:00)

You came here as a youth pastor. Yeah. In doing that, you have a set of beliefs that were well-defined before this. Has that been changed, altered, strengthened in any way this week? When we talk about all of these things like the evil entities and the guarding of yourself from these, you know. This is what Johnny's talking about, you know, especially with guarding yourself with what he does with sage and prayer and everything. (0:51:37)

I mean, the Bible talks about, you know, preparing yourself with the armor of Christ, you know. And that's, in my mind, that's the comparison I see. Be aware of what's going on underneath you, no matter where you are, you know. Because there might be some energy, some power that's there from way back, you know. (0:52:01)

Even our people don't know, because we're newcomers to this area. So our elders would always tell us, don't dig, don't do this, don't disturb things from the old people. There were people before us, so we didn't mess with that, you know. But do be aware of what's underneath you, you know. I've lived in cities, in Phoenix, in Chicago, and people build. And especially in Phoenix, there's been, there's probably thousands of cases building right over the Hohokam, you know, ruins and different things. (0:52:30)

And you have a lot of poltergeist activity around that area. But people don't know why, so I'll say. So know what's underneath you, know what's there, listen, don't disregard those stories, you know. And I think that's what's important. And that'll just enhance things, you know. It'll enhance you, because it gives you more history, more insight to what's going on. Because it's not just the past ten years since YouTube's been invented. (0:53:00)

No, we've been seeing this for a long time. But things are changing, I guess that's what I'll tell you. All our people say that. Just be prepared, things will get weird, things will change. You don't have to speak for the entire tribe, but would a weight be lifted in a lot of people if they could tell their side of the story? Yes. That's exactly what we had hoped to do by coming here. (0:53:30)

We hoped we could give voice to the experiences of those that had lived here the longest. Sometimes the campfire stories you hear end up being true. The next morning, anthropologist James Keenan, who had spent six years following the magnetic field shifts beneath the Uinta Basin, arrived at Space Wolf to take EMF readings. James' data and anthropological insight into an even older civilization added yet another layer of meaning onto the happenings we had experienced. (0:53:59)

In this area you have from a negative 14 microtesla all the way up to an 89 microtesla with the average for this area being a 46. I believe it was 46 for right here. So that's just what the magnetic differences are for each location in the earth all the way down to its core. A negative would mean that there's some type of cavity or void underground. (0:54:29)

The higher means there's something highly magnetic. To go up to an 89, you're talking about something like a large magnet. But what's insane is it's transient. It's moved. You can't have a negative 14 to an 89 in the same location, yet this is one of four spots that I've found and it's in a diagonal line. They perfectly match up at 8.34 degrees. And what's kind of crazy is that 8.34 degree heading goes right up to Blind Frog Ranch too. (0:54:57)

And then there's this whole underground cavern system too that we've been under in certain parts with a lot of flowing water. So we're wondering if maybe that's how, if it's highly saline, there's positive ions, high magnesium. (0:55:15)

My whole hypothesis is that there's some type of magnetic energy underground that's feeding to a relay. So you have point A underground, there's a point B, whatever that may be, and then it's transmitting out into space. And whatever it is, there's several Navajo symbols and there's actually a Navajo book that the front cover has the same type of theory. And it's all tied into the Yinaldluxi, which is a skinwalker. That's what the Diné call them. (0:55:49)

And also with the symbols of the petroglyphs and the pictographs, and then also obviously UFO. Yeah, the giants is a whole other topic, but you'll see that in the petroglyphs at Dry Fork Canyon. I mean, seven feet plus in height, six digits on the fingers, massively large feet. So they say the Citeka were the red-headed cannibal giants for this area. I don't believe they were cannibal, but they were headhunters. (0:56:20)

And you can see that in the anthropomorphic figures, or actually have taken heads, trophy heads. So that may be where that came from. Okay, that's interesting. I've heard of the red-headed giants before. And so now that we know we can visit somewhere where they were depicted, I think it would be worth our time before we head back home. Oh, absolutely. Even the three kings up at the top, you won't be able to get close, but with the camera you'll be able to zoom in. (0:56:46)

Consider the height factor of what you're looking at compared to what's around it. And there's one anthropomorphic figure over to the right. You'll see the patina is a lot older than the rest of it. It's truly an interesting rock art piece to look at, because that's just telling us that there was something about that site that was so important that it continued to be worked over and added to. (0:57:10)

And periods after. Had there really been giants here? How long has this high strangeness been going on? We did in fact find a number of petroglyphs left by ancient and little understood Fremont cliff dwellers near the basin. Ancient depictions of giants, shapeshifters, and even what some would call portals. With new layers of context on the basin, we gathered around coffee to prepare for our last night on the property. (0:57:39)

Going into tonight, I feel like my headspace is just more understanding compared to what it has been the past couple of days. Spending time with Johnny and Bo and understanding their culture, I understand a little bit more as to what kind of makes up this area and the essence of what's been going on. And we'll see what happens tonight with that. But I definitely feel like I'm coming from a more educated understanding. (0:58:08)

And as a result of that, I might go through an experience tonight that I might view differently than I would have two days ago. Yeah, I think I kind of have a patient mindset tonight. We came in kind of like guns ablaze and we were excited to get going. (0:58:25)

And now that we've had that experience with talking with both Bo and Johnny and others around the area, it kind of helps to settle that excitement down. But also knowing that we're in the presence of a lot of other things going on. So I'm pretty patient. Yeah, so for me, it's two things. One was last night around the fireplace when Johnny sat there and told us that he felt like that we've come in with reverence and respect. (0:58:54)

And he feels like the people that do that tend to see what they have come to see. Also, I think just from a perspective of who we are as a team, I think that's what we bring to the table. We don't come in here just trying to stir things up just for the sake of it. I think we want to go about it the right way. (0:59:10)

We want to do it in a respectful way and also a safe way. But I feel real good about tonight. I've been getting that feeling since I woke up this morning. And I know that place is just a hotbed ready to explode. Hearing the experiences of the people that lived here and having our own strange encounters earlier in the week, we were all excited for what our final night at Space Wolf would hold. (0:59:32)

Unfortunately, the night took a turn none of us expected. So back there when Jack was saying he saw that blue light blinking, which is obviously some sort of tower or something like that. As we were pulling past, I noticed there was a dirt road next to us and headlights lit up. And I said, well, that's kind of odd. They're on a dirt road. There's nothing back that way. (0:59:55)

And I started turning around and watching. And they slowly pulled out. They waited though for us to get way down. And they pulled out and they essentially followed us. And that's why I asked Tony to stop because it just seemed odd. I wanted to see what they did. (1:00:19)

Well, they did come by there, but they did slow up by the entrance to Space Wolf. But they kept going obviously because they saw us stopped. We didn't go all the way back to the campsite. So currently we are trying to follow them. Joseph just called me. So one of you guys could maybe call him. Yeah, somebody called Joseph. A truck hidden in the high desert had evidently been waiting for us to pass. (1:00:39)

When we pulled into the driveway at Space Wolf, the following car slowed to a stop at the gate. When they saw Joel get out of the vehicle and acknowledge them, they sped off. In the heat of the moment, we decided to follow. It looked like they sped up. I'm telling you, man, it's weird. There's no... It was like that classic... They were in the dark the whole time until we came driving by and then the lights lit up. (1:01:05)

Yeah. Well, that's odd how far out there he got. (1:01:12)

I know, he sped up big time. I have a feeling this guy is going to disengage on us. Keep an eye out left and right too. He pulled off. Yeah, look left, look left, look left. There are protectors. That's some good stuff. I mean, he's trying to tell me to turn, but... Careening down back roads at speeds of 90 or more, the car that had been following got away from us. (1:01:49)

During this chase, however, we got a call from Joseph back at our base camp. He had stayed behind that evening and so had seen that after we pulled out to chase the follow car, yet another vehicle had pulled into Space Wolf driveway and presumably would have continued all the way down to our campsite if Joseph hadn't flashed a strobing tactical flashlight at them. (1:02:10)

Get ready to text him that we're at the gate. You got it, Christian? Yeah. I've never seen a vehicle go around corners that fast though. That was that, like it's a pickup truck. Yeah, he was pushing it. He made distance on us. It's kind of hard to do that with as much stuff as what we have. Yeah, he got more weight. Yeah. We'll find out how far this car came down. Did it just come in here? (1:02:42)

Look at that though, you can still see the dust in the air. Yeah. I mean, that's what I thought when I saw that car pull up. The lights went off, all you saw was lights. When did you turn the lights on? Like right before you turned it in? So as it turned in, they went off before it completed its turn, rolled in, and I thought it was Chester's, a friend of Chester's or something. (1:03:05)

You know? And then he just kept coming, coming, coming, and I was like, oh no, no, no, no. Did it stop before you did that or after? No, it stopped when I did this. So like that stopped it? And then it backed up. Did it back up in a hurry when you did that? No. No, because I think it figured out how far I was away, but I'm thinking, what if those guys, whoever that was, a decoy, to pull you guys away and then somebody comes in here. (1:03:36)

Well, this car was like, I mean, I would just call it a Camry, that kind of car. Yeah, like a four-door. Could you tell Colin to turn it on? No, I couldn't, it was too dark. See that light? That's a motion sensor. That's the light that first alerted me to it, just as it like... So it's probably at 20, 30, or 60 seconds. (1:03:59)

There you go. There it goes. 30 seconds. Which means it kicked on. Being in a threatening situation put a massive damper on the final night. We became less worried about the unexplainable and more about our own physical security. Obviously, someone had wanted into our camp. (1:04:29)

But for what purpose, we don't know. Could there have been something we weren't supposed to know? Was it intimidation? Or just letting us know we were being watched? We did not bring the K2. Just saw it now. Do you think that there's ancient curses on this land, these lands and stuff, that might attract the activity that has been happening here? I mean, we're talking about upright walking dogs, giant wolves. (1:05:15)

We're talking about UFOs, abductions, rake-looking type creatures. There's so much going on here in this area. Do you think that there could have been an ancient curse put on this land that has been almost like a magnet for all this stuff? I didn't really know. I thought up until the point he was actually... I don't know if it was a he or a she. (1:05:38)

We were in the vehicle, and I don't even know exactly what it was, because I never got a full look at it. But it seemed like an interesting, possibly interdimensional type, now that I look back. But it was a very just... For all intents and purposes, what I saw was an older Native American in the middle of nowhere. Natives were very resistant to telling anything, because we didn't want to be diagnosed as crazy. (1:06:11)

That's true. So we kind of kept quiet and just kept it among ourselves. We didn't really talk until recently. But then at the same time, no one really asked us either. Could you define for the audience what a skinwalker is? I mean, there's a lot of people that define it differently, I've heard at least. But what would you say a skinwalker is? It is a mixture of things, and it really depends on what culture is defining it. (1:06:44)

Whether that be the Native Americans defining it as a skinwalker, or a dark arts practicing witchery way of following dark shaman, appears to be something they are not. Magic, perfectly explained, really. In the paranormal community, few places elicit as strong an association with the truly unexplained as this cut of high desert. Could it be that this place is set apart in some way sacred or desecrated? (1:07:20)

Why are experiences here so common, so vivid? Out at the margins of reality, questions abound while answers are rare. It's poetry, not a technical manual. What I do know, is that if you listen to the sounds that have hung over this place the longest, the voices of those with the longest memories, you can start to catch the rhythm. (1:07:43)

(2024-12-04)
